html:
The Avars were steppe nomads who ruled the Carpathian Basin, roughly modern Hungary, from 567 until about 800. They arrived from the east in the 550s, and in 567, together with the Lombards, they crushed the Gepids and settled the Pannonian plain. The Lombards then left for Italy, and the Avars had the basin to themselves.

Their ruler took the title khagan. From the plain they raided and squeezed the Eastern Roman Empire for gold, and in 626 they joined the Persians in an attack on Constantinople that failed. Many Slavs lived under their rule or fought beside them, and the Avar years saw the Slavs settle the Balkans.

After 626 their power slowly faded. In the 790s Charlemagne's Franks broke the khaganate and carried off its famous treasure. The Avars vanish from the records in the 820s, and a few generations later the Magyars took over the same plain.
